label: Scoping review protocol
framework: JBI scoping review guidance with PRISMA-ScR reporting fields

items.requirement: Identify the document as a scoping review protocol.
items.prompt: What is the full protocol title and how will it identify this as a scoping review?
items.helpText: Scoping review titles often signal mapping, concepts, populations, and contexts.
items.exampleResponse: Mapping digital adherence interventions for tuberculosis treatment: a scoping review protocol.

items.requirement: Explain why a scoping review is appropriate.
items.prompt: Why is a scoping review the right product for this topic rather than an effectiveness review?
items.helpText: Emphasize mapping concepts, evidence volume, knowledge gaps, or definitions.
items.exampleResponse: The field is heterogeneous and requires mapping before focused effectiveness questions can be developed.

items.requirement: State the review question using population/participants, concept, and context.
items.prompt: Define the PCC elements: participants, concept, and context.
items.helpText: PCC anchors scoping review eligibility and charting decisions.
items.exampleResponse: Participants: adults receiving TB treatment; Concept: digital adherence interventions; Context: low- and middle-income countries.

items.requirement: State the objectives of the scoping review.
items.prompt: What will this review map, clarify, classify, or describe?
items.helpText: Use verbs such as map, identify, describe, summarize, and classify.
items.exampleResponse: We will map intervention types, delivery channels, settings, outcomes measured, and reported implementation barriers.

items.requirement: Specify inclusion criteria aligned to PCC.
items.prompt: Which participants, concepts, contexts, evidence sources, and publication types will be included or excluded?
items.helpText: Scoping reviews may include diverse study designs, reports, guidelines, and grey literature.
items.exampleResponse: We will include empirical studies, program reports, guidelines, and conference abstracts addressing digital adherence support.

items.requirement: Describe information sources and search coverage.
items.prompt: Which academic databases, grey literature sources, organizational websites, and reference lists will be searched?
items.helpText: Include sources that capture unpublished or non-indexed evidence.
items.exampleResponse: We will search MEDLINE, Embase, Global Health, Web of Science, WHO IRIS, program repositories, and reference lists.

items.requirement: Describe the search strategy and iterative refinement process.
items.prompt: How will the search be developed, piloted, and refined during the scoping review?
items.helpText: JBI scoping reviews commonly use iterative search refinement.
items.exampleResponse: An initial limited search will identify keywords and index terms, followed by comprehensive database searches and reference screening.

items.prompt: How will records be screened, how many reviewers will participate, and how will uncertainty be resolved?
items.helpText: Specify title/abstract and full-text screening procedures.
items.exampleResponse: Two reviewers will pilot screening criteria, screen titles and abstracts, and resolve disagreements through discussion.

items.requirement: Describe data charting variables and process.
items.prompt: What information will be charted from each source, and how will the charting form be piloted?
items.helpText: Use charting language rather than effect-estimate extraction when appropriate.
items.exampleResponse: We will chart publication details, population, setting, intervention features, outcomes, implementation barriers, and evidence gaps.

items.requirement: State whether critical appraisal will be conducted.
items.prompt: Will sources be critically appraised? If yes, which tools will be used? If no, why not?
items.helpText: Critical appraisal is optional for many scoping reviews, but the decision should be explicit.
items.exampleResponse: We will not conduct critical appraisal because the review aims to map evidence rather than synthesize effectiveness.

items.requirement: Describe plans for collating, summarizing, and reporting results.
items.prompt: How will the mapped evidence be summarized visually, numerically, and narratively?
items.helpText: Mention tables, maps, taxonomies, categories, and narrative summaries.
items.exampleResponse: Results will be summarized with frequency tables, evidence maps, and narrative synthesis organized by intervention category.

items.prompt: Will stakeholders help refine the question, interpret findings, or identify grey literature?
items.helpText: Consultation may strengthen interpretation and relevance.
items.exampleResponse: Program implementers and patient representatives will review preliminary categories and identify additional sources.
